_comment: Real estate vertical value chain + supporting sectors, per the GOAL spec. rateSensitivity is qualitative judgement (provenance 'added' unless noted), linkedFactors reference factors.json ids.

chains.name: Real Estate Vertical
chains.source: User-specified chain structure (GOAL spec), stage detail added/researched

stages.name: Raw materials & commodities
stages.rateSensitivity: Medium -- prices mostly follow demand, not rates directly. But when rates slow construction, demand for these materials falls too.

stages.name: Building materials & equipment
stages.rateSensitivity: Medium -- demand follows construction activity, which slows when borrowing gets expensive.

stages.name: Engineering & architecture
stages.rateSensitivity: Medium-High -- one of the first things cut when new projects stop getting approved.

stages.name: Construction
stages.rateSensitivity: High -- loan costs and demand for new space both move directly with rates.
mainDrivers: Development spread (yield on cost vs cap rate)

stages.name: Property development
stages.rateSensitivity: Very High -- scores 9.0/10. This is the most rate-exposed step in the whole chain.

stages.name: Real estate ownership
stages.rateSensitivity: High, but it depends on the segment -- Office and Residential are most exposed, Property Management the least (see the Heatmap view for detail).
mainDrivers: Cap rates vs risk-free rate (Rates factor)
stages.source: research.pdf -- WHERE MY RESEARCH IS NOW (user-specified)

stages.name: Property services & operations
stages.rateSensitivity: Low -- scores 1.8/10, the lowest of any step. These are fee-based businesses, not asset owners, so rates affect them less directly.

supportingSectors.name: Banking & Finance
supportingSectors.rateSensitivity: Very High -- this is how rate changes actually reach the rest of the chain.

supportingSectors.name: Insurance
supportingSectors.rateSensitivity: Medium -- insurers actually do better when rates are higher, but rising premiums (partly due to climate risk) squeeze property owners' profits.

supportingSectors.name: Utilities & infrastructure
supportingSectors.rateSensitivity: Medium -- energy prices feed straight into the cost of running a building.

supportingSectors.name: Investment & capital markets
supportingSectors.rateSensitivity: Very High -- REIT share prices are set by comparing their dividend yield to government bond yields, so they move with rates directly (p.5).
supportingSectors.source: research.pdf Rates factor, GOVERNMENT mechanic, p.5
